1363.9: Chaubole, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O Samman, if this love could be had in exchange for money, then those like Ravan, he who cut off (his) heads and offered them (to Shiva), were no paupers. ॥1॥
Chaubole: a form of verse whose stanzas are spoken to particular hearers, here Sikhs named in the lines: Samman, a Sikh of Shahbazpur, his son Moosan, and Jamaal.
Ravan: the demon king of Lanka in the Ramayana; by tradition he cut off his heads one by one and offered them to Shiva to win his favour.
1363.10: The body steeped in love and affection keeps not a mustard seed's distance (from the Beloved); the mind is pierced by (his) lotus feet; this is understood when the awareness is joined (to him). ॥2॥
1364.1: The oceans, Mount Meru, wilderness and forest, and roaming over the nine regions of the earth: O Moosan, on the path of the Beloved's love, I count (all this) as a single step. ॥3॥
Meru (Sumer): the golden mountain at the centre of the world in the Puranas. The nine regions (khand): the earth as the Puranas divide it.
1364.2: O Moosan, the moonlight of love has spread over the sky; pierced (by love) and bound within the lotus, the bumblebees stay clinging (to it). ॥4॥
1364.3: Recitations, austerities, self-restraint, delight, comfort, honour, greatness and pride: O Moosan, for a single moment of love I would sacrifice them all, offering them up again and again. ॥5॥
1364.4: O Moosan, the world, dying and being robbed, does not know the secret (of love); it is not pierced by the Beloved's love, and is caught up in false dealings. ॥6॥
1364.5: When home and wealth are burnt, (one) is wretched, torn from what (one) loved; O Moosan, one is (truly) robbed only then, when the merciful Being is forgotten. ॥7॥
1364.6: Those whose aim is love keep (the Lord's) feet in thought within (their) minds; O Nanak, those who pine for God (Brahm) go nowhere else. ॥8॥
1364.7: Climbing very high over lakhs of hill passes, the fickle mind is wretched; O Jamaal, the mud is lowly and very humble: by (this) conduct the lotus (grows in it). ॥9॥
1364.8: (The Beloved has) lotus eyes (lined) with dark collyrium, a face like the moon, a lovely mind; O Moosan, absorbed in (his) mystery, break the necklace to pieces. ॥10॥
1364.9: (The moth) is absorbed in the love of its beloved (the flame); remembering (it), it is unaware of its own body. O Nanak, the lowly moth has become known in all the world. ॥11॥
